changelog.change: Rebuilt the hint ladder: deleted the length rung, added a category rung at cost 1 and a meaning rung at cost 3 either side of the existing first-ezhuthu rung at cost 2, and added categoryLabels holding the Tamil tag the category rung renders for each lexicon category slug.
changelog.why: Row 14 of the lexicon pipeline - the length rung charged one point for the tile count already on the player's screen, and offering it as one of two hints short-changed the player. The ladder is walked in order rather than chosen from, so its order is its pricing and the three rungs now escalate in what they return as well as in what they cost: a tag, then a letter, then a phrase. categoryLabels lives here rather than in copy.json because hint wording lives here - the Tamil templates already do - and the lexicon's categories column holds English slugs, since a category is a machine dimension there. A slug with no label has no rung: a ladder that is sometimes two rungs is correct.

changelog.change: Added themeEveryNDays and gave the anagram generator its first themed wordlist.
changelog.why: Row 15 of the lexicon pipeline - a themed set nothing draws from is a dataset nobody reads, so the day loop needs a place to find one. A theme is registered per Game beside its ordinary wordlist, and the day runs it only when a whole playlist can be drawn from it. themeEveryNDays is 7 because the theme is wide enough to fill months of consecutive days, and a Daily that is nature every day for a season is the opposite of the variety a theme exists to add; one themed day a week is also the cadence the theme's growth target was sized against.

changelog.change: Gave every difficulty band a maxStratum bound alongside its length bounds, and moved the length bounds to 3-4 easy, 4-5 medium, 5-6 hard.
changelog.why: Row 12 of the lexicon pipeline - difficulty is two-axis, because length alone is anti-correlated at both tails: a long Tamil headword is usually a compound that decomposes and is easier than its tile count suggests, while a short rare word is brutal. The old easy band was minLength 3 / maxLength 3, which forced the generator into the shortest words - disproportionately literary, and brute-forceable at six arrangements against three attempts. Bounding easy to the most familiar quarter is also what makes it impossible for a day to be three words nobody knows.

changelog.change: Initial daily-engine registry: the anagram generator, its difficulty bands, and its hint wording.
changelog.why: Row 13 - the daily puzzle engine is a separate layer from the corpus, so its knobs are a separate file from the runtime app config.
